what: The rest of tropical_file_vintage at the d091673 cut: every row but the heartbeats (which the d091673 bank already holds), as Postgres's own row_to_json(t)::text, one row per line, in vintage_id order; with the heartbeats it is the whole ledger at the cut. The routes read three of its products for `corrected` (fcst_5day_zip and fcst_radii_zip, the files the official points are parsed from, and pws, the odds; pantry ingesters/tropical_bank.py); the rest is banked so the local table is the size Neon's was and is planned as Neon plans it. Read-only through the Neon connector, 2026-10-10 12:00-12:07Z, in 10 reads by vintage_id range.
cut_rule: fetch_ts <= cut AND product <> 'heartbeat': the d091673 bank's own cut, so the ledger and the points it describes are one instant. All 2,637 rows are status banked with closed_ts null (the only column the bank ever UPDATEs, and only on pending/absent rows); a banked row is never updated (pantry d091675), so reading it a day later returns what stood at the cut. 13 are anomaly copies (meta.anomaly_prior_sha, the d091675 events); none carries meta.correction. 36 rows are of the three products the routes read.

dataset.columns: dataset_code, lifecycle_status, refresh_cron, freshness_mode, stale_after_override, enabled (the ledger rows' datasets the d091673 bank does not hold: atcf_deck_vintage, nhc_advisory_vintage, nhc_two_vintage, nhc_wsp_vintage)

ddl.ddl_294.sql: pantry migration 294 sections 1-2 (revision in both keys, the three views), applied after the rows
ddl.ddl_297.sql: pantry migration 297 (ttp_revised, tpo_revised, the two views with q.revision > 0), applied after 294

constructed: corrected.sql: the constructed corrections (R1-R5); applied only by the tests that ask for them, never by the bank load
sha256_rule: as d091673's: Neon computed encode(sha256(convert_to(string_agg(row_to_json(t)::text, E'\n' ORDER BY vintage_id), 'UTF8')), 'hex') in the statement that returned the rows; the suite recomputes it on every load. Written by tests/fixtures/tropics_d091673/bank_from_neon.py.
chunks: ledger in 10 reads (vintage_id 10-274, 275-539, 540-808, 809-1073, 1074-1337, 1338-1603, 1604-1868, 1869-2131, 2132-2401, 2402-2677); the sha over the whole text was computed by Neon in one statement; bank_from_neon.py reassembled and checked it before writing
